bodyText:
For eleven years, Alpha twins and an entire pack bullied me while I hid behind baggy clothes and silence. But when they dragged me into a battle ring with a silver whip, I realised I could not keep holding back. Then my father's betrayal finally unleashed my wolf, and I fled to another pack. Why are the people who destroyed me suddenly terrified of losing me? 📖
Chapter
Athena POV
“I used to think my life was a tragedy, but now I realize, it’s a comedy”. 
That famous quote from the Joker runs through my head over and over, as my clothes are absolutely drenched in slimy red and yellow gunk. 
Only, in my case, it’s still a tragedy. I fail to see the comedy part in all of this. 
I smell like an omelet gone bad. No - an omelet gone bad months ago. Everyone in the cafeteria is snickering or downright bellowing in laughter, at my expense. And why shouldn’t they? It’s their handy work that I’m covered in rotten eggs and goddess knows what after all. Welcome to my life.
Sadly, I have gotten somewhat used to the bullying. I have learned a long time ago that firing back only makes things worse. And, well, it’s just me against the world. Or at least against my own pack. The teachers don’t even bother trying to stop it either. One of them tried 2 years ago, and she was fired and sent packing on the spot. 
Courtesy of the 2 identical Alpha pricks that enjoy making my life a living hell. Who, by the way, finally graduate this summer. The goddess must have finally taken some pity on me after all. And no - they aren’t smarter than me. Just 1 year older. How they managed to graduate at all is beyond me though. Saying they aren’t the brightest crayon in the box wouldn’t do them justice. They don’t seem to have any functioning brain cells at all. 
As you can tell, I hate them with fierce determination.
They have ensured my life is a living hell since I was 6, and sometimes I honestly wonder why I haven’t given up yet. If only I weren’t such a stubborn b*tch, I might have. Who knows. I like to hope there will be a turning point at some stage. 
I don’t know what I have ever done to deserve torture to this extent, but the moon goddess must definitely think I do. I pray to her every day that my mate, if I will get any, will be from red runner pack. And I say “if I will” for a reason – but I will get to that later. 
I visit red runner every summer, and have done so ever since I was little. And I have actually made friends there. Even with the Alpha heir, Maxim, and the beta’s daughter, Millie. 
‘You made 2 friends. 2. Not friends, as in plural’ Ares snickers, to which I just scoff. ‘That was just rude and uncalled for’ I reply back snarkily.
Okay, maybe I’m not exactly a social butterfly. At all. In fact, if I wouldn’t have to hold back so much, people might call me a sarcastic little shit instead. 
Well, let me introduce my wonderful life to you (yes, sarcasm in the third degree). 
I’m Athena Brooks. Yes, Athena, you read that correctly. Courtesy of my father, who wanted a fierce name for his little baby. Or so, the official story goes. But, I will get to that later too.  
My naming after the Greek goddess of warfare, heroism and courage has been an endless supply of ammo for my bullies throughout the years, I’ll tell you that. That and my, and I quote, “whale size body”. 
Anyway. I’m from blood moon pack, where the vermin of werewolves reside. I am 17 years old and finally turning 18 next summer, a few months away. Finally of legal age to do as I please. 
Well, sort of. I don’t know what I am going to do after my 18th birthday yet, but I don’t think I can stay here. Especially when the 2 shit stains would take over the Alpha position after their father in a few years’ time. The current Alpha, their father, is a complete dickhead as well. But at least he doesn’t go out of his way to target me and make my life a living hell, like his precious sons enjoy doing so much. 
It hurts my heart to think of leaving mom behind though. But I don’t see myself ever escaping the pit of doom I am in otherwise. 
‘Melodramatic much, geez’ Ares pipes up again. 
Ah, yes, I almost forgot - I have my spirit animal already. I say spirit animal for a reason, and once again I will get to that later as well. She too has a fierce name. Ironically enough, considering we are very docile.  
‘Not by choice, though’ Ares grumbles. And rightfully so. We have been threatened with my parents’ wellbeing more times than we can count. They know exactly where to hit to keep me in check.
‘We’ werewolves always get our wolves at the age of 18. We share our body and soul with them going forward. But, Ares came to me when I was 6. We have never actually shifted into our wolf form though, after my mom made us swear on her life that we wouldn’t. We found it strange, and we still regret not being able to shift, but my mom won’t relent. Every time I try to bring it up her eyes fill with panic, and she keeps insisting it isn’t the right time yet. I’m not sure if there will ever be a right time in her eyes though. What good is it being a shifter, if you’re not allowed to shift? 
I think my mom is scared that I will turn out not to be a wolf, but something like a squirrel, or a mouse. Which brings me to another tidbit of information about me. Apparently, my mom isn’t my biological mother. And neither is my “father”. Although I am not too peeved about the latter, considering I have no relationship with the man whatsoever. My mom stung for a while, but she loves me like her own and has always given me everything a mom should. So, I can only applaud her for that. 
She explained how she was in the last semester of her own pregnancy, when she sadly lost her baby. She was wandering around in unclaimed lands. And, as if it were divine intervention, she came across a woman seeking refuge for her baby. The woman was dirty, with matted hair, torn clothes and a frantic look in her eyes. 
My mom took one look at me, one look at my crazed biological mother, and decided she couldn’t leave me with the woman. The woman gave my mom some basics about me, and that’s it. That’s all she wrote.
Mom’s story still haunts my nightmares though, although I would never tell her that. She would feel guilty for telling me, and I don’t want that. She is an absolute angel. And although I don’t know how to feel about my biological mother, my mom is everything to me. I would lay down my life for hers in a heartbeat. Which is exactly how the shit stains and their posse got such a hold on me. Pricks.

Chapter
Athena POV
Anyway, back to my spirit animal, who I am just going to assume is a wolf until proven otherwise. Why she came this early I have yet to figure out. Perhaps the moon goddess sent her early as a way to deal with my pathetic life. It was beyond a little confusing when she came to me. I thought I was going batshit crazy. 
‘Going?’ she teases. Since we share a soul she can hear every thought I have. Ares is a cheeky one, I’ll tell you that. Damn feisty too. Whatever I’m lacking, she has in redundance. 
Confidence being one of those things. Being bullied your entire life will do that to you, I guess. Along with trust issues to last me a lifetime. I don’t even trust Millie 100% yet, afraid anyone will turn on me once I let my guard down. 
That’s the way it went with the shit stains as well. We were actually best friends at some point. One day we were all fine and playing together, and the next day, like the flip of a switch, I was stamped as the pack’s doormat. 
I still can’t grasp in my mind what happened. But I have stopped trying to decipher it. It is what it is. I have been called every name in the book, but fat-ass seems to be their favorite pet name for me. Lucky me, huh? 
Sure, I used to be on the thick side for a werewolf, but that all vanished when I got Ares and when I started training at red runner one summer, together with Maxim and Millie. After that, I kept my training regimen secret back home as I don’t want any of them to see me working out. I still solely wear sweatpants and baggy clothes outside of my home, as their constant belittling is still gnawing at my confidence. 
I have long brown hair, but I always put it in a bun. And most of the times I wear caps. Why bother, right? And it feels comfortable.
Millie has been urging me to let go of my bun and baggy clothes more, but I haven’t found the desire nor courage for it yet. I just hope my mate can look past it in due time and love me for who I am. If I get a mate, that is, considering I don’t know for sure what I am yet. 
I wonder if I will get a wolf mate if I turn out to be anything else, since I am living with them. I would have hoped to have found him already. But then again, I only ever visit red runner pack. I’m just praying my mate is from there, since I absolutely adore the pack. You can only find your fated mate, blessed to you by the moon goddess, when both parties have their wolf already. 
Anyway, I trailed off. Back to Millie. Millie has become my absolute best friend. The feisty redhead is an absolute diamond. Bright and pure. I have told her and Maxim bits and pieces of my life here, but not all of it. I’m afraid they’ll judge me for it. 
Alphas tend to stick together. Even though Maxim seems genuinely different from the terror twins, also known as Jake and Jerry. But I prefer to call them shit stains. Or rats. I too have my pet names for them. But, naming them rats is an insult to rat species really. 
Besides the rat boys, we have cockroach Thalia, who is a warrior’s daughter. The nickname cockroach suits her more than I can put into words. I call her that because she really is the most disgusting creature to ever walk this earth. I know it sounds horrible, but really, you should meet her. 
She has platinum blonde hair, smooth skin and her body is thin. She looks hot, absolutely perfect. Don’t you just hate it when someone has it all? Besides her personality, that is. Or any personality at all, I should say.
I don’t even hate her with determination anymore. What I feel for her has no bounds. My blood boils when thinking of her, and I feel an overwhelming urge to squash the life out of her whenever I see her. 
‘So much for being docile, huh?’.
I do love how she always hangs off Jake and Jerry when I’m near though. Like I am any threat to her at all, like I would want anything to do with either of them. B*tch, there’s not enough money in the WORLD for me to want to have anything to do with them. Ever.
You know those women who are so insanely sweet, forgiving and loving that they end up protecting or even caring for their lifetime abusers?
Yeah – that isn’t me. Tit for tat bro.
I have been forced to submit in the past years, yes, mainly because of their incessant threats to hurt (the livelihoods of) my family. But the fire inside me hasn’t nullified. On the contrary - it’s a raging inferno by now. I just shove it down deep enough to not emerge. 
Anyway. Then there is bed bug Benji. He is the future beta, considering the chauvinistic pricks here decided a woman can’t be a ranked member, and my “father” only had a daughter. And lastly there is mosquito Brody (the gamma’s son). This sums up the worst of them. 
Their entire posse consists of 8 to 10 of my bullies, but these are by far the worst. The rest of them seem to just go with the flow. Not that that makes them any better. 
Although I have resided in my fate in order to protect my family, Ares is the total opposite of that. Each beating, each humiliation, each time our head gets shoved down the toilet until we pretend to pass out ignites her fire even more.  She wants to rip them all to shreds. And, honestly, she easily could since they have no wolves yet. 
And I still believe she is a wolf considering how fearless she is. Wolves are at the top of the food chain. She wouldn’t be this bold against wolves if she wasn’t a wolf herself. It is a bit odd that she is this fearless in front of the Alpha heirs though, knowing we could be severely punished or even executed if we ever acted upon her murderous thoughts towards them. Wolves are generally submissive to their Alpha.
But mom was adamant on not shifting when she saw Ares’s red eyes. You see – red eyes aren’t normal for a wolf. They have black eyes once the wolf pushes forward. The only other person that has seen them is our Luna Grace. Yes - the mom of those shit stains. In the beginning, when I wasn’t so skilled at controlling my wolf yet, she saw my eyes flash when I was being bullied and couldn’t control Ares for a split second.
When she too insisted I kept it a secret, with a slight panic might I add, I started putting more effort into suppressing Ares. Grace is a great luna and an amazing person, so I took her words to heart. It’s ironic that she is such a kind person, since she is the mother of the kings among scum. 
Unfortunately for me, she doesn’t carry much weight in this pack, since our pack is misogynistic as can be and the luna is seen as a glorified party planner. Luna Grace is so much more though. At least to me she is. She is the only one besides my mom who gives a damn about me, and I have come to love her. 
Anyway. I have glanced at Ares’s eyes in the mirror when she was pushing forward. And my goddess - she has the most breathtaking, extraordinary red eyes. 
It has made me question several times whether or not Ares is indeed a wolf. But, like I said, I just can’t imagine her being anything less considering her fierce nature. In fact – I believe she is a bit more.. special than the average wolf, considering the color of her eyes. Maybe that’s why mom doesn’t want us to shift.
Ares does agree to not let others in the pack see her though,  despite her wanting to rip them to shreds every day. She told me her instincts were also telling her not to reveal herself in our pack. She is just really bad at containing her anger unfortunately, as am I.  I have to close my eyes each time someone angers me or Ares. 
Needless to say, I almost spend my days like a blind person with having to close them so much. 
I am brought back rudely from my thoughts when another rotten egg hits me square in the eye, and I curse under my breath. Glancing up, I see Jake grinning like a hooker who just got spanked. 
Did I tell you I hate them with a passion yet? 
Ares lets out a low growl, but not loud enough for them to hear without their wolves. Next to Jake stands Jerry, with a demonic grin on his face as well. When my gaze drops to his hand, I spot why he is grinning. And, on cue, a dead rat (oh, the irony) is hurled at me. 
I. Fucking. HATE. Them. SO. much. 
Closing my eyes for the umpteenth time today, I wonder why the moon goddess doesn’t descend and strike them down on the spot. I would do anything to see that happening, I would definitely sacrifice a kidney or something.
‘Just let me free and I’ll do the dirty work’ Ares growls. But we can’t, and she knows it. F*ck my life. She just has some anger management issues at times like these. Although I don’t blame her. I would gladly scratch their eyes out myself. 
So, let me elaborate on the vermin before me as a distraction to keep my mind occupied. Because of their Alpha blood, both of them have muscles and jawlines for days. All Alphas do. They have black, wavy hair almost reaching their shoulders, and brown eyes meant to draw in any woman they please. 
Anyone except for me, that is. 
I am about the only girl in the pack they haven’t slept with. The only plus side of being labeled the pack’s degenerate.  It’s fucking gross if you ask me. I pity the girl that will be mated to them. The fucked-up part of it all is that women not of Alpha blood are unable to reject their fated mate if he is an Alpha. Poor girl. I can only hope that the girl they will be mated to is equally disgusting as they are. Someone like Thalia. 
I pray to the goddess that my fated mate won’t be such a man whore. Or such a filthy human being. I don’t know what I would do if he were. Sure, appearance wise they are handsome. But that doesn’t balance out their repulsive personalities. Typical “pretty on the outside, rotten on the inside” story. 
“OH MY GOD, LOOK AT HER FACE!!! I’M DEAD” I hear the cockroach bellowing out in laughter, taking short gasps of air in between. 
‘I hope she chokes on her laughter’. 
‘Me too, Ares. Me too. Or on a bag of d*cks’. I sigh in response. 
This is my life, welcome to the shit parade!

Chapter
Athena POV
After everyone has returned to their seats in the cafeteria, still laughing, I move my way back towards the hallway where the restrooms are. 
“Well, the fat fuck can easily miss a lunch or 50”. I hear Jake bellowing out in laughter. I clench my jaw and grit my teeth, doing everything I can to prevent myself from letting Ares free. 
F*ckkkk me, I can’t wait to get out of here one day. 
‘Or rip their throats out, eat them, maim them, burn them, drown them. All those options would be good for me’. Damn. 
Deep in thoughts and not paying attention to my surroundings, I bump into something. Hard. To my surprise however, the object I bumped into speaks up. 
“Ouch! Watch where y… Oh my god, Athena!”. The voice rings in my ears like a melody, a soothing balm to my soul. I would recognize that voice anywhere, belonging to my best friend Millie. What I don’t understand however, is what she is doing here, in blood moon? In my school. All packs have their own schools, so Millie doesn’t attend mine. Before I can ask however, she seems to notice my appearance and smell. 
“Goddess, what happened to you?!” she gasps, to which I just sigh in return. 
“Surprisingly, nothing new” I offer a small smile, shrugging my shoulders. Oops. I let that slip without thinking about it. “More importantly: why are you here?!”. 
“What do you mean nothing new?”. Her brows furrow and I can tell she is getting upset, with the way her jaw ticks ever so slightly. When I don’t respond, she sighs and pulls my hand to drag me to the nearest restroom. “Let’s get you cleaned up first!”. 
“Yeahhh, the restroom isn’t going to cut it. I need to grab clean clothes and head to the showers in the gym” I respond. Having experienced this treatment before, I know anything beside a shower and clean clothes won’t do. 
As we reach my locker and I open it to take clean clothes out, Millie starts to explain she transferred to our pack for the year as a sort of exchange student. Although I am thrilled to see her, I am already dreading the inevitable outcome. She needs to stay away from me if she wants to have anything resembling a life here. 
Sighing, I drop the message. 
“Millie, you need to stay away from me”. I can’t see her facial expression considering she is behind my locker, but I can hear her temper shining through in her tone of voice. Millie is mostly a gentle giant, or at least to me, but she can have quite the temper as well. 
“Why the hell would I do that?”. She replies aggravated. 
“I… You…”. I try to formulate a sentence, but nothing comes out. Next I hear is a whistle coming from behind my locker, just as I am retrieving the last of my stuff. 
“Damn, who are you?”. 
“I don’t believe we have met”. 
I shut my locker, but groan upon hearing the shit stains voices. Luckily, however, their attention is not on me, but on Millie. Millie smiles, oblivious to the fact that she is smiling at the twin devils themselves. Them trying to hit on her was to be expected though. Millie is beautiful. A part of me had just delusionally hoped I was able to keep my best friend a little longer. 
I try to sneak off silently, but Millie’s eyes land on me just as I am about to break away. Shit stain #1’s eyes follow her gaze, and his eyes harden immediately as they land on me. The contrast in his expression when he looks at Millie versus when he looks at me is like day and night. 
“What are you still doing here, fat-ass? Get the fuck out of here”. He sneers at me, and I continue walking away without another word. 
This is the moment I have always dreaded. Millie is going to realize what a loser I am, and dump me like a ton of bricks. Just like everyone here has. I have always known it was inevitable at some point. But I still feel a pang of hurt, even though I tried to shield my heart and tell myself not to get attached anymore. 
Stupid. I am so stupid. 
After a few seconds I hear them call out. “Hey! Where are you going?”. 
I’m confused, but I don’t look back. Curiosity is killing me when I hear several bystanders gasp though. Fast footsteps approach me, and I speed up my pace too, rounding the corner towards the showers. Before I reach them, I am shoved against the wall, facing an angry Millie. 
I am telling you, this lady can be scary if she wants to be. Even though we are even in normal combat, something about the intensity in her eyes makes me shrink. 
“What the hell was that?”. She raises her voice at me, and I flinch a little at her harsh tone.
“What do you mean?”. I ask, utterly confused. “Look, Millie, you’ll come to see I am not someone you want to be friends with. Especially not here. Just g…”.
She interrupts me swiftly. And quite rudely, might I add. I might be the pack’s laughing stock, but I have manners. Geez. 
“Did you hit your head or something? Why the hell didn’t you defend yourself?”. 
I look at her dumbfounded with my brows furrowed. Did she not hear me or something? Ironically, her expression looks equally dumbfounded as mine must look to her. Only a lot angrier. 
“Why would I have hit my head?”. 
“Jesus, Athena!”. She throws her hands up in the air in frustration, pacing back and forth. “I have seen you fight, Athena. And I know you are even holding back with me. You could easily wipe the floor with them”. 
Well, I could, but I can’t exactly say that. She doesn’t know I have my wolf already. And besides that, I can’t tell her about them blackmailing me. She would surely try to fix things, and get my family hurt unintentionally.
“No I couldn’t, Millie, they are the Alpha’s sons”. 
She scoffs at me. “They don’t even have their wolves yet, Athena!”. 
I feel a pang of nervousness rise, what does she mean by that? 
“Neither do…”. I was about to lie through my teeth, but she interrupts me yet again. 
“Bull f*cking shit Athena! I have seen your eyes flash!”. She exclaims angrily, before adding in a hushed tone. “Red, might I add….”. 
I gulp nervously, before panic starts to set in. “Millie, please, you can’t tell anyone!”. I plead with her, clutching my hands together in a praying motion. 
She grumbles, before responding. “I haven’t, now, have I?”. She taps her foot impatiently, while I am pondering on her words briefly. 
“Well, no.. Not yet at least”. I mumble under my breath, barely loud enough for her to hear. 
“I don’t get it though, Athena. Help me understand. You have an extraordinary gift and you are an amazing fighter, why let them bully you like that?”. 
“Well I can’t fight the entire pack now, can I?”. I snap at her, immediately regretting it when I see her facial expression is full of sympathy. “And besides, do you know what they would do to a female attacking the golden Alpha boys? In a misogynistic shithole like this one?”. She remains silent, studying my face. 
“So, well, unless you want to lather up my body in soap, I am going to hit the shower now. Alone”.

Chapter
Athena POV
 “I will wait for you right here” she nods, seemingly still deep in thought and not noticing the pointed look I am giving her at all. 
3 rounds of scrubs later, I can still smell the rotten eggs on me. Perhaps those without a wolf might not smell anymore. But those who do have their wolf definitely will. Lucky for me nobody in school has their wolf yet, except for the teachers of course. 
Saves me some grace, huh?
‘What grace? You have the grace of a bulldozer’. Ares snickers. I can’t blame her, I kind of do.
Stepping out of the shower, Millie is still in the exact same spot I left her. She looks troubled, but also.. fired up. Normally, I love that look on her. But now, when it could mean my demise, not so much. Much to my bewilderment though, she doesn’t say anything. Yet.
“Let’s get to class. Which ones do you have?”. I ask.
“I don’t know, which ones do you have?”.
“My roster will be different from yours, everyone has different courses”.
“Nope, I have all the same you do. Specifically requested it. And after that shitshow back there, I’m even more glad about that”.
“Wait, you asked to share all my classes? And they simply just.. gave it to you? Oh goddess, you are so going to get me killed here”. I groan.
“Alpha Menno may have pulled some strings here and there. Even though you are not his pack member, he cares about you, you know? And come on, grow a pair Ath! Where the hell did the firecracker I have come to love go?”.
“She was beaten into submission”. I laugh, but Millie doesn’t seem to find it amusing. If I’m being honest, they haven’t beaten me into submission. Just.. compliant, I guess. For my mom’s sake. “Let’s go snowflake”.
I grab her hand, and start pulling her back towards the hallway.  Have to admit I feel a little lighter knowing she isn’t dumping me just yet.
Just my luck though - the bell rings at the exact moment we enter the hallway. Yugh. I tense up for the onslaught Millie is going to witness. Millie though, being the absolute angel she is, squeezes my hand. Her shoulders are squared, and she walks with a level of confidence I can only dream of. I admire and adore this woman so much. Too bad we can’t mind link each other. Mind linking is a way to communicate telepathically with people inside your pack, when you have your wolf. 
As always, everyone starts grinning and chuckling the second they see me. If only they knew I could rip them all to shreds if I wanted to. If I hadn’t promised my mom I wouldn’t show Ares, and if I wasn’t afraid of retribution against her. So many “ifs”. 
As soon as they spot Millie, however, their chuckles and grins die down. Due to my wolf hearing, I can hear them whispering to one another.
“Who is she? And what is she doing with that thing?”.
“The exchange student is hot as f*ck. Bad choice in company, though”.
“Someone should tell her she needs to stay away from the fatty”.
As much as I try to tell myself I’m numb to everything by now, and that I don’t care what anyone else thinks, it still stings. Not as much as it used to, thank goddess. But, nobody likes to be this despised by literally everyone.
‘F*ck them. F*ck them all! I’ll rip their throats out and burn this pack down to the ground one day’. Ares seethes. Like I said – she has some anger issues. But, admittedly, I feel the same. I would take mom, luna Grace and – despite our issues – dad, and leave the rest to burn. 
“Hey girl! You’re the exchange student, right? I’m Thalia, the Alphas’ girlfriend. Come with us, you don’t want to be seen with this one”. The cockroach laughs, with her friends snickering along with her. 
Millie tenses up instantly. Looking at her face, I’m certain she would growl and show her teeth if she could. She lets go of my hand, and for a split second I still worry if she has finally come to her senses about her friendship with me. 
“YO, ALL OF YOU, LISTEN UP!”.
“Millie, don’t!”. I whisper yell at her, looking around frantically.
“Yes, I am the exchange student. And I have ZERO interest in any of you being my friend. ESPECIALLY you, I don’t do bedwarmers for friends”. She looks Thalia dead in the eyes. “How utterly pathetic. One of the Alphas’ toys thinks she is special. Until they find their fated mate, goddess help the poor soul, and you will not even be a lingering memory”. She laughs, and I wince at the onslaught that is bound to follow.
“Now, all of you, stay the f*ck away from me if you know what’s good for you. Y’all have a fabulous day now”. She calls out, before grabbing my hand and dragging me to class. Normally, I would have sarcastically commended her for at least wishing them a fabulous day. But I am still in shock I guess.
The shock wears off quickly however, when Millie gets pulled back by her arm abruptly. It’s one of Thalia’s little minions, considering the b*tch herself seems to be too stunned at the moment.
“YOU B*TCH!”. The little tit screams, raising her hand to slap Millie.
And, right at that moment, something snaps inside of me. 
I don’t care what they do to me, I’ll live. But nobody touches someone I love. I don’t care if you were an Alpha, or even the f*cking king. Nobody touches her.
Before Millie can make a move, I have moved to place myself in front of her already, intercepting her hand by grabbing her wrist firmly. 
“What the…”. The little tit starts to seethe, but I cut her off. She didn’t see this coming, that’s for sure. And why would she? I have never once fought back. 
“You do NOT touch her, do you hear me?!”. I squeeze her wrist just a little, causing her to scream out in pain. ‘P*ssy’. Ares comments dryly, and I have to agree with her. I barely used any strength at all. 
“NOBODY TOUCHES HER!”. I yell a little louder than I intended to. But, I guess you could say the anger I have bottled up all these years is surfacing since they tried to touch Millie. “NOBODY!!!!!”. I yell once more, glancing around the hallway with a deadly glare. 
When my eyes land on the 2 shit stains, my anger spikes, and a snap rings through the air. 
“AHHHHHHHHH!!!!”. The little tit screams, and I hear gasps coming from all around us.
“That’s enough, babe. You’ll get in trouble”. Millie whispers into my ear, and I let go of the wrist of the little tit. 
“Who cares? School sucks anyways”. I reply more composed than what I am feeling on the inside. Millie grabs my hand and drags me away. I can feel their piercing gaze never leaving me, until we round the corner, out of sight.
“Well. Happy first school day!”. I smirk at Millie, before realization what I have just done sets in. I just.. feel so different when I am with Millie. And when I am at Red runner pack. My insecurities don’t gnaw at me so badly with her, and I feel… srong sometimes. I don’t know if that’s a good thing, or a bad thing. Bad I guess, when you combine it with my protective instincts towards her.
“I just signed my own death warrant, but, hey, it was fun while it lasted, huh?”. I chuckle.
“That was SO badass! That’s the girl I know!! And the hell they will. If they even so much as touch you, they will have to go through me”. Yeah. It’s not them touching me what I am so afraid of. Let’s hope the little tit is insignificant enough to not earn the shit stains wrath. 
“I know. But, you won’t be here forever, unfortunately”.
“Maybe you won’t either”.
“With my luck, I will”. I scoff.
“Maybe your mate is in Red runner” .
“Maybe. But I doubt that somehow”.
Millie gives me a side hug as we round the corner to our classroom. When we enter, we seem to be the first to arrive. I normally sit at the front, but Millie drags me all the way to the back.
“Better vantage point”. We both say in unison, laughing as we walk to our seats in the left corner. 
Other students start to pour in, each and every one casting a dirty look my way. 
“Freak”. I hear one of them whisper, followed by some others and their whispers. I try to tune them out as much as possible.
“Alright, class”. Our history teacher comes walking in. I can’t quite put my finger on it, but something about his aura is… off. He looks different. And when he starts to speak up, I know exactly why that is.
“A last-minute adjustment to the course of today has been brought to my attention. Follow me”. His eyes connect with mine briefly, and I can read something that looks like mild panic in them. Whatever is going to happen, it’s not good. We never leave the room in this class.
“Field trip?”. Millie asks excitedly, but I don’t share her enthusiasm.
“Something like that”. I respond absentmindedly, while getting up from my chair. “Whatever happens, DON’T interfere Millie. I mean it”.

Chapter
Athena POV
“Huh? Why would something happen?”. She asks, her brows furrowed in confusion. The poor, naïve soul. I am glad she has no idea what I’m talking about though. It means that red runner treats their pack members a lot better than they do here. Not that I expected anything else, based on the summers I have been there all these years.
I don’t respond, despite her continuous tugging on my arm in an effort to get me to talk, while we walk through the hallway. The teacher stops at the gym, a hardened look on his face. Yep, I knew it.
‘Let’s just f*ck them up!’. Ares growls in my mind, knowing what is going to go down as well.
‘We can’t, you know that. We’ll live. They’re not even that strong, you know that too’.
Ares doesn’t respond anymore, but I can feel her anger rising with each step we take. I, however, have already resided in my fate. This isn’t my first rodeo. And I knew right after bruising her wrist already that something like this was going to happen. It’s nothing short of what I am used to. Or so I thought, until I enter the gym.
‘They are really going for the kill this time’. I tell Ares, while looking around the gym. As expected, a battle ring has been set up. What is new this time though, is not only that the 2 shit stains are in there themselves looking battle-ready, but also the silver whip I see #1 holding. 
Oh, shit. Silver is like kryptonite to a wolf. That will hurt and scar like a b*tch. So far, anything they had done healed up in no time, without any scars. But this time, I won’t be so lucky.
“ATHENA BROOKS. ENTER THE RING FOR YOUR SPARRING SESSION”. #2 booms out, and for a split second I contemplate just getting the f*ck out of here. But, I wasn’t born a quitter, am I right? All jokes aside – I have to take the punishment. They’ll hit me harder, where it really hurts, if I don’t. 
“Ath, you don’t have to do this! I can bring you back to Red runner, you know Maxim will take you in”.
Actually, I don’t. Alphas usually don’t take members from other packs in, for any other reason than having found their mate. Regardless, my mom is in this pack. I’m stuck.
“It’s OK, Mills. Nothing I’m not used to. But, I’ll take it as a good training”.
“THIS IS NOT TRAINING! This is 2 alphas against 1 girl, using f*cking SILVER WEAPONS! Ath, please..”.
“It’s OK, Mills. Don’t intervene”. I tell her, before I start moving towards the ring. Millie starts calling out to me. When I glance back, I see she is being restrained by 4 men. She is thrashing and screaming wildly. And, despite my predicament, I laugh at the fact that they need 4 men to restrain 1 girl. That’s who Millie is.
Stepping into the ring, calmness washes over me, oddly enough. There is nothing they can do to break me. I just need to sit this out one more year.
The fist hitting me square in the jaw a second later, however, makes me doubt that for a split second. They have rarely put their hands on me themselves. They usually let their minions do the dirty work for them. They never fail to mention it’s because they don’t want to contract any diseases from me. I guess this time they found it worthy enough to risk it regardless.
Blow after blow is raining down on my face and my torso, the ferocity and hatred behind them clear as day. One of the rats before me kicks me in the abdomen, causing me to fall flat on my back.
Blow after blow continues to hit me, and I can feel my face starting to swell. I close my eyes, knowing Ares will try to push forward any second now. 
“FIGHT THEM, ATHENA!”. Millie screams, the panic evident in her voice. She doesn’t understand though. If I fight back, things will only get worse. Which I would be able to take, had it been only about me. But they have threatened my mom and dad before as well. Not physically, but they have threatened to remove my dad from his position. Which would devastate both mom and dad. We would have no income. And now Millie is a target to hurt me with as well. 
The little f*cks have me right where they want me. Cornered, and they know it. 
Another hard blow connects with my face. And this time, I hear a crunch. I wince, but I refuse to let them hear me scream. I never have, and I never will. I would die before giving them the satisfaction of hearing me scream. A hard kick to my chest pushes the air straight from my lungs, and I am struggling to breathe for a second. F*ck. Who knew the pussies could actually throw a punch?
I roll over, onto all fours. This position always helps to get more air into my lungs when I need it. Gasping for air, I hear Millie scream before something really sharp tears through my clothes and skin on my back.
‘Let me out, Athena!’. Ares roars. ‘I will rip them apart!’. 
More long, deep slashes follow. I wonder how long they are going to keep this up. Sure, they have done about everything in the book to me. Waterboarding included. But it has never been this bloody thus far.
Cool air hits the gashes on my back, offering little relief to the wounds. They will heal, but they still hurt like a b*tch. Just when I think this is over and done with, I hear the crack of the whip. And not long after, I feel the lash on my back. It doesn’t hurt as much as the gashes from the knife or whatever it was they used. Which is quite surprising. Silver is our kryptonite, I should be screaming in agony.
Lash after lash, I feel the whip cutting deeper and deeper into my already existing wounds. Each time it hits, blood gets splattered all around me. At one point, I wonder how much blood I have left in my system. I am starting to get dizzy.
“WHY WON’T THIS BITCH SCREAM?!?! SCREAM, YOU FAT F*CK!”.
Shit stain #1 yells at the top of his lungs, but I refuse to scream. Like I said - I will drop dead before I give them that satisfaction. And I meant it. 
“Jake, Jer, stop! She’s about to die, man! Millie will report you to the council, and you will get your titles stripped!”. Bedbug Benji sounds panicked, and silence befalls the room. Although I’m still dizzy, I can feel the healing has begun to set in already. Which is weird, considering they used silver. Huh. 
“F*ck, he’s right”.
I can hear them whispering among themselves in a mild panic now. And who would I be, if I didn’t take full advantage of that?
3… 2… 1… action.
Dropping myself to the ground, laying lifelessly, I keep as still as humanly possible. I even manage to slow down my breathing, in case anyone were to check. Guilt consumes me when I hear Millie scream, however. I hadn’t thought about her also seeing this.
‘She will understand’.
“THAT’S ENOUGH! NURSE!”. Our history teacher now yells, and I hear fast footsteps approaching me. I didn’t even know he was still here. Despite knowing that his job would be on the line if he defied them, I still think it’s scandalous that teachers are allowing this to happen. Pathetic.
Only when I am on the ground lifelessly, does he step in. Too little, too late amigo.
** 2 hours later ** 
“It’s so strange... She has healed almost completely already. When she came in, I… I wasn’t quite sure she was going to make it”. I hear the nurse whisper in the hallway. I am not sure to whom, however.
“Huh…”. The other voice responds. It’s a male at least, I can tell that much.
“It’s almost like she has her wolf already, Alpha”. 
Oh, crap. The Alpha is here. He won’t be here to wish me well. 
“That can’t be. The girl isn’t of age yet. And she isn’t strong enough”.
“What if she has a special wolf?”.

bodyText:
I caught a guest stealing from my cat boarding facility last Tuesday.

When I called her she was already crying.

Don was 11. Eight pounds. Vomiting almost daily for three years.

Four days here without a single vomit.

She couldn't let it end.

If your cat has been on prescription food for months and keeps vomiting anyway — what she stole is exactly what you need to know about.

My husband Marcus and I have been running a small cat boarding facility for the past 6 years. Five-star reviews, 28 private rooms, climbing trees, the works. We've boarded hundreds of cats — picky eaters, hider-under-the-bed cats, the one who learned to open his room door on the second night.

Normal stuff.

But about 8 months ago, something started happening we'd never experienced.

Clients started asking about the small jar on the feeding station counter.

I keep a small wellness station there — water bowls, a few approved treats, and a glass jar filled with an unflavored powder. A handwritten card says: "Daily taurine sprinkle — one scoop on her food. Great for boarding cats during a stressful stay."

Most clients let us add it to their cat's bowl the way they'd let a hotel add a turndown mint. It's hospitality. Nobody thinks twice about it.

But the pickup conversations started shifting.

"I don't know what you fed her but the smell is gone from her litter box. What was in that jar?"

"He hasn't thrown up once since we got him home. Three days. That has NEVER happened. What did you do?"

"She's been playing with toys she's ignored for two years. What's actually going on?"

I knew what was in that jar. I'll explain why later. But what I didn't expect was clients noticing early changes during a four-day stay — and bigger ones in the weeks after. It took my own cat over a month to show full results. I figured a few days of taurine wasn't enough to move the needle for anyone.

I was wrong.

The comments kept clustering around the same things. Vomiting stopped. Litter box smell gone. Energy back. Eating full bowls without leaving half. That wasn't the boarding stay. That was the same shift I'd seen happen once before — in my own kitchen.

One couple booked their 13-year-old back the following month because the wife said her cat hadn't thrown up in three weeks for the first time in years. A retired teacher extended her cat's stay by two days because her cat had eaten a full bowl without backing away from it halfway through. She watched her cat eat through the window of her room like she was watching a different animal.

Something was happening. Something real.

Then last month, something happened that still keeps me up at night.

A woman named Diane dropped off her cat Don on a Thursday. Mid-60s. She was warm, organized — the kind of energy where you could tell she was the one who held everything together. But Don the cat was the one who broke my heart. He was 11 years old. Used to be 14 pounds. Now he was 8. Vomiting almost daily, she told me. Three different prescription foods. Two rounds of dewormers in the past year. The vet kept saying "he's just an old cat."

They left Don with us for four nights.

On pickup morning, Diane was right on time. Paid. Thanked us. Carried Don out in his carrier.

But when I went to clean the feeding station, the jar was gone.

I pulled up the camera footage from the feeding station — disclosed camera, standard facility security.

There it was. 6:47 AM on pickup morning, before we'd unlocked the front door. Diane had come in through the side entrance to grab Don's carrier early. She walked to the counter. Looked over her shoulder. Picked up the jar. Wrapped it in one of her cat's towels. Put it in her tote bag.

She took the whole jar.

My first reaction was frustration. The next guest was arriving in four hours and I'd have to drive 30 minutes to my house to grab more from our pantry.

But that frustration lasted about ten seconds.

Because I thought about the retired teacher watching her cat eat through the window. The couple who booked again. Every pickup conversation from every client who'd watched their cat get one scoop of powder and walked out with the first hint of a cat they'd been missing for years.

This woman watched her cat for four days. And whatever happened to him — or to her — was enough that she couldn't leave without it.

That's not theft. Not really.

That's someone who found something and was terrified of losing it.

I texted her: "Hi Diane — hope Don settles back in at home. I noticed the jar of powder is missing. Everything okay?"

Forty-five minutes later, my phone rang.

She was crying. The ugly kind. The kind where someone has been holding something in for a long time and it finally comes out.

"I'm so sorry," she said. "I know it was wrong. I'll pay for it. I'll pay you whatever you want. I just —"

She stopped. Took a breath. Started again.

"Don has been on prescription food for almost three years. Hill's i/d. Every six months we go in and the vet says 'we're managing it, just keep doing what you're doing.'"

Her voice got harder.

"But he is NOT managed. The vomiting started slowly. Once a week. Then twice. Then almost every day. Yellow bile in the morning. Undigested food in the afternoon. I've been cleaning vomit off my carpet for three years."

"Then the weight loss. He went from 14 pounds to 8. I can feel every rib through his fur. But he keeps eating. He BEGS for food. Then throws half of it back up an hour later."

"The litter box was so bad I had to keep the bathroom door closed. My grandkids stopped coming over."

"His vet says he has a sensitive stomach. The vomiting? 'That's just Don. He's an older cat now. It happens.'"

Her voice broke.

"It's not just aging. I've had cats for 30 years. Something is being taken from him. And nobody will listen to me."

I was gripping the phone so hard my knuckles were white.

"That powder on your counter," she said. "I didn't know what it was. You sprinkled it on his food Thursday evening. He ate the whole bowl. He didn't throw up that night."

"Friday — nothing. Saturday morning he threw up a little, but nothing all afternoon. Sunday — nothing. By the time I came to pick him up Monday morning, I realized something. The daily vomiting that I'd been cleaning up for three years had basically stopped. Three days with almost nothing."

She was sobbing now.

"And then this morning, just before pickup, I watched you sprinkle one more scoop into his bowl. He ate it. He looked up at me. And I knew. I knew that was the difference. I knew if I left that jar behind, he'd be throwing up again by tomorrow."

"I panicked. I knew it was wrong. I took it anyway. Because for the first time in three years, I'd seen what he could be without the vomiting — and I could not let that end."

I was crying too.

Sitting on the floor of my own feeding station, tears running down my face, listening to this woman describe my own life back to me.

Because two years ago, I was Diane.

My cat Marigold started vomiting at 9 years old. The vet called it a sensitive stomach. Six months in, she was on prescription food. The vet was thrilled with how she was "managing." And every morning I sat in my kitchen cleaning bile off my floor.

The details were different but the shape was the same. Marigold lost her appetite, then started begging — and threw it all back up. Her litter box smelled like death. Her vet said "she's just getting older." Same script. Same dismissal. Same woman sitting across from a vet knowing in her bones that something else was happening.

What I need to tell you is what I found when I went looking for answers. Because that's the part nobody told me. And it's the reason that powder is on my feeding station counter.

One night — 1 AM, couldn't sleep — I was at the kitchen table with my laptop. Marigold was asleep on a folded towel on the kitchen floor. Not because she wanted to be. Because that's where I'd put her after she'd thrown up and I'd cleaned the mess and she was too tired to move.

The cat I'd had for nine years used to sleep on my pillow. Now she couldn't make it to the bedroom. And the vet called it aging.

I started researching. Not "best food for sensitive stomach." I'd already wasted months on that. I researched WHY. Why was her stomach failing?

That's when I found a long post on a feline health forum. Written by a retired veterinary nutrition researcher. Twenty-eight years of practice. He'd left the field because he said he couldn't keep recommending diets that he now understood were causing the very problem he'd spent his career trying to manage.

His writing was precise. Clinical. Not angry — just tired. Like a man who'd spent three decades doing something he'd finally realized was wrong.

He started by explaining what's actually happening inside a chronically vomiting cat.

"Up to 75% of cats are carrying parasites their owners can never see," he wrote. "Indoor or outdoor, premium-fed or not. The eggs are everywhere — on shoes, in dust, on a fly through a screen. Most owners assume their cat is safe because she stays inside. She isn't."

"Cats have a built-in defense against this. The liver produces a powerful bile acid that dissolves the protective shells around parasite eggs before they can hatch. Every egg that walks into a cat's body is supposed to be destroyed in her stomach. Before it ever takes hold."

"But that bile acid needs one specific nutrient to be produced: taurine. Cats can't make it on their own. No taurine, no bile acid. No bile acid, no defense. And every parasite egg that walks in walks right through her stomach untouched."

I thought about her shrinking spine.

"Here's what they don't tell you. Commercial cat food destroys 50 to 70% of the naturally occurring taurine through high-heat processing. And if the food is grain-free, the peas and lentils inside bind up whatever survives the heat. So your cat is eating a food labeled 'complete and balanced' — and her body is starving for the one nutrient her parasite defense needs to function."

That was exactly what Marigold's vet had done. Switched her to prescription food. Told us she was "managing." Checked the box.

Then this researcher wrote something that made me physically sick.

"With no bile acid to destroy the eggs, parasite larvae hatch in her intestines. They burrow into the gut wall — physically tearing through the lining where food is supposed to be absorbed. The damaged gut becomes chronically inflamed. Food can't pass through properly. And the cat throws up."

"This is why chronic vomiting in cats is so often misdiagnosed as 'sensitive stomach.' The cat IS sensitive. But not because of the food itself. Because there are parasites tearing through her gut and the bile defense has been disabled by the very food she's eating."

My hands were shaking.

"This is why dewormers fail. They kill the worms inside today. They do nothing to fix the broken defense. The eggs already in the home — they can live in carpet for years — just wait for the medication to wear off, then walk back into a defenseless gut and start the cycle over."

I looked across the kitchen at Marigold. Asleep on the towel. Bony. Exhausted.

Her vet had never tested why the vomiting was happening. Not once. In two years. Every six months they checked weight, said "we're managing," and sent us home with another bag of prescription food.

They were watching the wrong thing. While the real damage built up where nobody was looking.

"The question becomes: if the broken bile defense is the actual driver of chronic vomiting, what fixes it?"

"Standard supplementation fails because most cat taurine on the market is bound to fillers, heat-damaged, or so under-dosed it never reaches the liver. What works is pure free-form taurine — the molecule itself, pre-digested, absorption-ready. It bypasses the damaged food chain entirely. Reaches the liver intact. Restores bile acid production within days. And once that bile is back, the parasite eggs entering her body get destroyed on contact again. The way her body was designed."

I read that paragraph three times.

This researcher had walked away from a 28-year career because he'd watched cat after cat deteriorate on diets that managed a symptom while the real damage continued underneath.

I closed my laptop at 3 AM. Opened it again at 5.

I found the product he'd referenced in a follow-up post. Pure pharmaceutical-grade free-form taurine. Unflavored powder. 98.5% purity. Third-party lab-tested every batch. You sprinkle one scoop on her food once a day. The taurine is absorbed directly — no heat damage, no legume blocking, no degradation in storage.

I ordered a jar that morning. KittySupps.

Marcus thought it was just another supplement I was trying. I didn't argue. I just sprinkled it on Marigold's food that evening, set the bowl down, and watched.

She ate the whole thing.

She didn't throw up that night.

By the end of the first week, the daily vomiting had slowed to maybe once. By week two, the smell from her litter box was completely normal. I cried into a roll of paper towels in my kitchen because for the first time in two years I wasn't using them to clean up bile every morning.

By week four, Marigold had gained back almost a pound. She started jumping on the kitchen counter again — something she hadn't done in over a year.

By week six, I took her to the vet.

The vet read the numbers to me. Weight: 8.4 to 11.2 pounds. Up almost three pounds in six weeks.

She was quiet for a while. Then she said: "I don't know what you changed. But whatever it is, keep doing it."

She didn't refill the prescription diet.

That was ten months ago.

Marigold's been off the prescription diet for nine months. Weight stays at 12 pounds. She hasn't thrown up in over six months. Her litter box smells like litter. She sleeps on my pillow. She jumps on the kitchen counter at 5 a.m. demanding breakfast instead of vomiting on the floor.

She's the cat I had before any of this started.

A few weeks after Marigold's vet visit, I filled a glass jar with taurine powder. Wrote a card. Set it on the counter at the boarding facility next to the food scoops.

Didn't overthink it. Just did it.

That was eight months ago. And those pickup conversations I told you about at the beginning? Now you know why they don't sound like normal boarding feedback.

Because it's not just feeding routine.

It's what gave me my cat back.

So here's what I told Diane on the phone that day:

"Keep the jar. But let me send you the link so you can order your own. Because that jar will run out. And when it does, I don't want Don to go back to the way he's been."

She laughed through her tears. "Deal."

I sent her the link that afternoon. She ordered three jars.

Last week — exactly three weeks after their stay — she texted me a photo.

Don on top of the bookshelf in their living room. Eyes bright. Belly filled out. Looking down at the camera like he owned the place.

Five words underneath the photo:

"I have my cat back."

That's the message from the beginning of this story. That's what made me cry.

If you're reading this, I know where you are.

You've been watching a cat you love disappear. The body that used to be 12 pounds. The appetite that used to be steady. The cat who used to sit on your pillow, jump on the counter, eat a full bowl and walk away satisfied.

And the vet keeps saying she has a sensitive stomach. The chart looks fine. Keep feeding the prescription food.

But the chart isn't the one cleaning vomit off the floor. You are.

You've been treating the wrong thing. The whole time.

One path: keep buying the prescription food. Keep cleaning vomit off the carpet. Keep watching her lose weight, sleep through the day, hide under the bed. Keep hearing "she has a sensitive stomach" while you know in your bones it's something else.

Another path: rebuild the bile defense the food has broken. Restore the taurine her body can't make on its own. Watch the vomiting stop. Watch the smell disappear. Watch HER come back.

I chose the second path. Diane chose the second path.

Marigold is living proof. Don is becoming proof.

I don't know how to rate that. Five stars isn't enough." Marcus read it over my shoulder and squeezed my hand. If your cat is vomiting and you've been watching her dim — the bile in the morning, the smell from the litter, the bony spine, the cleaning routine you've built your week around — the powder on my counter is KittySupps. That's what Diane took. That's what Marigold eats every morning. That's what I sprinkle into every boarding cat's food.

I keep three jars in the house now — one for Marigold, one backup, and one for the facility. If your cat's next vomiting episode is tomorrow morning and you want to walk into your kitchen and find a clean floor for once — check if they have stock today. Not next week. Now. If men hit perimenopause at 38, there would be no such thing as "too young" in a doctor's office.

I am 41. 

The first time I told my GYN that something was wrong with my body, she told me I was too young to be in perimenopause and to come back if it got worse. 

It got worse. I am writing this because I do not want any other 38-year-old to be told to wait.

========

I'm 41. I have a six-year-old. I run marathons. I work in product management.

 By every metric anyone would use to describe a person in her prime, I am in mine.

Except for the part of my body that decided early retirement was its own idea.

It started at 38. A mild dryness during intimacy. 

By 39 it wasn't mild anymore. 

By 40 intimacy had become something I scheduled around discomfort instead of around desire. 

By the time I was 40 and a half, I had stopped initiating, then stopped wanting to initiate, then stopped wanting at all.

I went to my GYN in the spring of last year. I was 40 and shaking in her exam room. I had a list. 

Painful intimacy. Vaginal dryness no lubricant fixed. Vanishing libido. Brain fog. Mood swings. 

The growing certainty that something was deeply wrong.

She asked one question: "Are your periods regular?"

I said yes.

She said: "Then you're too young for perimenopause. Come back when something is actually wrong."

========

I left her office crying in the parking lot. I did what every woman in our generation does next: I went on Reddit.

Within forty minutes I had read fifty stories from women in their late thirties and early forties who had gotten the exact same dismissal. 

Too young. Periods regular. Come back when it's worse.

It was, statistically, almost all of us.

========

For the next nine months I tried everything that a woman in early perimenopause is told to try by people who are not paying attention.

A naturopath put me on adaptogens. They did nothing.

A different GYN put me on a low-dose birth control pill. It made the brain fog worse.

A pelvic floor physical therapist gave me dilators and a series of exercises. 

The exercises helped a little with one symptom and nothing with the rest.

A men's-health magazine that my husband subscribes to ran an article about Viagra adoption rates rising for men in their thirties. 

The article was 4,000 words. There were three case studies. The men were 32, 35, and 38. They were taken seriously.

I had been told, at 40, that I was too young for my own body's signals.

========

The breaking point came at a baby shower.

It was a friend's second baby. Half the women in the room had recently had children. 

Half were a few years past it. Several of them were quietly going through their own version of what I was going through. 

We were all wearing the same dress in different colors and we were all carefully not telling each other the truth.

After the cake my friend Nadia pulled me into the kitchen. 

Nadia is 44. She is the kind of friend who notices what is in your face that you have been hiding from your own mirror.

She said: "What's going on with you?"

I told her. The bathroom in my GYN's parking lot. The nine months. The nothing.

She put down her wine glass and said: "Okay. I'm going to tell you what nobody told me at 41. 

The problem is that almost nothing on the consumer market is designed for our bodies in this stage. 

The traditional toys make it worse. 

The lube makes it sticky. The advice is condescending. There is one thing that actually works. I'll text you the link."

She texted me a link. The link was Nancy Lem.

========

I went home and read everything.

Air-pulse, not vibration. Soft suction. The mechanism is fundamentally different. 

It restores blood flow to thinning tissue without rubbing it. The lowest setting feels like breath. 

It is designed for the bodies that the wellness industry has stopped designing for.

I read the science: in early perimenopause, estrogen begins fluctuating wildly. 

Blood flow to the area decreases. Tissue thins. Sensation drops. 

The "use it or lose it" advice has merit, but only if "use it" means the right kind of use. 

Friction makes things worse. Pressure waves do not.

I read the reviews. The reviewers were 38 and 41 and 47 and 59 and 71. 

They had been told the same thing I had been told, in different doctors' offices, in different decades.

I ordered one.

========

 Inside the box was a small yellow lemon-shaped device, a magnetic charger, a pink storage pouch, and a card that said: Air-pulse, not vibration. Twelve settings. Start at one.

========

Day 1. I started at setting one. The motor was so quiet I could hear my own breathing in the bathroom. 

The first sensation was so gentle I almost reached to turn the device up. 

I stopped myself. The card had said start at one. I stayed at one.

Day 3. I had natural moisture for the first time in eighteen months.

Day 7. It happened in the bath. I had not released in two years. 

I lay in the water afterward and cried because I had been told, at 40, that I was too young for the thing my body had been telling me about.

Day 14. I had intimacy with my husband for the first time in nine months without bracing first. He noticed.

 He did not say anything. He held my hand at breakfast the next morning.

========

I am 41. I am back in my own body. The doctor who told me to come back when it got worse was wrong. 

So was the second doctor. So was the third.

I do not want any other 38-year-old to spend nine months thinking she's broken because the medical system has set the bar for "real" perimenopause at the wrong number.

If you are 38 and your GYN told you to wait, you do not have to wait. The thing that worked is $89.

bodyText:
If a man's body started shutting down five separate functions at the same time, no doctor would call it normal at your age.

I had five separate doctors call mine that. Across two years. 

With a straight face. Each.

I am writing this because I am almost certain that you, reading this, have at least three of those visits in your own past.

========

I'm 51. 

I have been a woman with health insurance and a good job and a primary-care provider and an OB-GYN and a willingness to advocate for myself for almost three decades.

None of that helped me when, between 47 and 49, the following six things began happening to my body in roughly this order: 

hot flashes I dismissed for a year, painful intimacy I dismissed for two, dryness no lubricant fixed, brain fog at work I started writing post-its about, 

sleep that became unreliable around 3am, and a numbness during intimacy that, by 49, was the symptom that scared me the most.

I went to five doctors. 

I did not get the right answer until the fifth.

========

The first doctor was my OB-GYN of twelve years. I described the painful intimacy. 

She told me to use coconut oil. I asked about the dryness. 

She told me dryness was common at my stage. I asked about the numbness. 

She said it was probably stress. I asked her if it could be perimenopause. 

She said: "Are your periods regular?" I said yes. She said: "Then no."

The second doctor was a urologist my OB-GYN sent me to. 

He spent eight minutes with me, prescribed a topical estrogen cream that did nothing for the numbness, and made a small joke about the wear and tear of marriage that I am still annoyed about.

The third doctor was a primary-care physician I switched to after the second one. 

She took me more seriously. She ran a hormone panel. 

She told me my numbers were within normal range for my age and recommended a couples therapist. 

I told her my marriage was fine. She suggested an SSRI for the brain fog. 

I left her office wondering if I was going crazy.

The fourth doctor was a different OB-GYN, this one specifically advertised as menopause-trained. 

She charged $400 out of pocket.

 She listened for forty minutes, which was the longest a doctor had listened to me in two years. 

Then she said: "I want to be honest with you. 

At your age, with these symptoms, my best advice is to manage your expectations."

I went into the parking lot and cried for fifteen minutes before I drove home.

========

The advice I had been given over two years and roughly $1,800 of co-pays and out-of-pocket consultations was, in summary:

coconut oil

a topical estrogen that did nothing for the underlying issue

a couples therapist for a marriage that was working

an SSRI for brain fog that turned out to be perimenopause

"manage your expectations"

That last one is the one I want every woman reading this to hold onto. manage your expectations. 

That phrase is what the medical establishment says to a fifty-year-old woman when it has run out of tools and is not willing to admit that the toolbox was never built for her in the first place.

It is not advice. It is a formal apology disguised as a recommendation.

========

The breaking point came on a Saturday hike.

My friend Joelle and I had been hiking the same loop for six years. 

Joelle is 54. She had been through her own version, three years ahead of me. 

She had not pushed me. I had not asked.

That Saturday, on the second mile, I broke. I told her about the four doctors. The painful intimacy. The numbness. 

The manage your expectations. I cried for most of the third mile. She let me.

When we got to the top she sat me down on a rock and said: "Okay. Three things."

She said: "First. Drop your current OB-GYN. She is not going to help you. 

The fact that you have seen four doctors and only one used the right phrase is evidence of where the medical establishment is."

She said: "Second. The 'manage your expectations' line is a confession. 

It means they have no tools. It does not mean tools do not exist. 

It means the tools they were taught about don't apply to you."

She said: "Third. There is a tool. It does apply to you. It is $89.

 I bought one two years ago and have been waiting for you to be ready. Today is the day you are ready."

She reached into her pack and pulled out a pink storage pouch.

 She had been hiking with it for six miles. She had been carrying it the whole time.

========

She walked me through the science on the way down.

Air-pulse, not vibration. The mechanism restores blood flow to thinning tissue. 

Decreased blood flow is the underlying physiology behind most of what I had been describing — the dryness, the painful intimacy, and especially the numbness.

The "use it or lose it" advice has merit, but only if "use it" means the right kind of stimulation. 

Friction-based toys irritate already-thin tissue. Air-pulse does not.

She said: "Your fourth doctor told you to manage your expectations because the only tools she knows about would have made you worse. 

There is a tool that would have made you better. It is not in her training. It is in our group chat."

She said: "My second OB-GYN — the menopause-trained one — also told me to manage my expectations. 

I bought the Lem the same week. 

Six weeks later I went back to her and told her, on the record, that I had not in fact managed my expectations and would she like to know what worked. 

She listened. 

She has now recommended it to forty patients. She emailed me last spring to thank me."

========

I bought one that night. It arrived in a box on a Thursday.

 I read the card. I plugged it in. I locked the bathroom door.

Day 1. Setting one. Sensation without pain for the first time in three years.

Day 7. Natural moisture. 

The thing my OB-GYN said was common at my stage and the urologist treated with a cream and the third doctor wanted to medicate with an SSRI

 all of those treatment plans had been treating the wrong target. 

The right target was blood flow.

Day 21. It happened in the bath for the first time in I don't know how many years.

========

I went back to my fourth OB-GYN three months later.

 I told her I had not managed my expectations. I told her what worked.

She listened. She wrote it down. She said: "I'm going to start asking my patients about this."

I do not know how many of them she has asked. 

I know how many I have told. Joelle told me.

 I told my sister. My sister told her best friend. 

We have a chain that goes back, by my count, eight women, and it is the chain I now trust more than the medical system.

========

I spent two years and $1,800 and four doctor visits being told to manage my expectations. The fix cost $89.

End the gaslighting with Nancy Lem.

🛁 Waterproof.

🤫 Whisper-quiet.

While you are looking for one, buy the Lem. 

The new doctor will take six weeks to find.
